    Translation

    2865. Ṣāliḥ b. Ṣāliḥ b. Ḥayy, with an alternative genealogy inserting Muslim between Ṣāliḥ and Ḥayy; another form is Ḥayyān, and Ḥayy is Ḥayyān's nickname. He may be ascribed to his father's grandfather as Ṣāliḥ b. Ḥayy or Ṣāliḥ b. Ḥayyān. Aḥmad said, 'Trustworthy, trustworthy'; sixth generation; died in 153 AH. Al-ʿIjlī declared him trustworthy but graded the aforementioned Ṣāliḥ b. Ḥayyān al-Qurashī as weak. This is the correct distinction. [ʿ.]

    Taqrīb al-Tahdhīb no. 2865, ed. ʿAwwāma, p. 272

    Translation

    2892. Ṣāliḥ b. Nabhān al-Madanī, client of al-Tawʾama (with fatḥa on tāʾ, sukūn on wāw, followed by hamza with fatḥa): truthful, but suffered confusion late in life. Ibn ʿAdī said there is no objection to the reports transmitted from him by earlier pupils such as Ibn Abī Dhiʾb and Ibn Jurayj. Fourth generation; died in 125 or 126 AH. Whoever claimed al-Bukhārī included him was mistaken. [d, t, q.]
